key_insight: The paper proposes a distribution-agnostic reinforcement-learning layer that robustifies a nominal trajectory using affine feedback while enforcing chance constraints from sampled rollouts.
engineering_relevance: It offers a reusable stochastic-control scaffold for mission design that can handle different uncertainty models without needing a distribution-specific reformulation.
method: Compute a deterministic nominal trajectory offline.
Learn feedforward corrections plus time-varying feedback gains for closed-loop robustification.
Use rollout-based upper-tail quantiles and covariance penalties to preserve probabilistic feasibility and terminal dispersion bounds.
evidence_signal: The framework is evaluated on two distinct problems—a 3D Earth-Mars multi-impulse transfer and a stochastic rocket landing case—under Gaussian, uniform, and unseen disturbance conditions.
watch_item: Feasibility is enforced empirically from sampled rollouts, so performance may depend on sampling coverage and may be sensitive when deployed outside the training disturbance set.
paper_title: Distribution-Agnostic Robust Trajectory Optimization via Chance-Constrained Reinforcement Learning
